root_idea.summary: The root develops three principal semantic branches: greatness or exalted status, fortune or prosperity, and cutting or separation.
root_idea.development: The cutting sense extends to what is newly cut or newly made, hence “new”; to visible stripes or paths marked off from their surroundings; and to dry or severed things such as a milkless udder. The branches of majesty and worldly fortune remain distinct lexical developments.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized adjective جَدِيد.
Displayed as the distinct noun جَدّ.
The Quranic plural جُدَد is displayed under the supported singular citation form جُدَّة.

senses.definition: New; newly made, brought into existence, or restored.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Quran for things characterized as newly made or newly constituted, including the renewed creation associated with resurrection.

senses.definition: Divine greatness, majesty, or exalted status.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the Quranic expression concerning the exalted status of the Lord in 72:3.

senses.definition: The divine effusion or bounty proceeding from God.
senses.usage_conditions: An interpretive Quranic sense of جَدّ in 72:3, presented as a divine outpouring or beneficence rather than simply majesty.

senses.definition: A visible stripe, band, or tract distinguished from what surrounds it.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural جُدَد in 35:27 describes conspicuous differently colored bands or tracts on mountains.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cut or cut off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The primary transitive sense; it may refer to cutting cloth, palm fruit, or part of an animal's body.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become fortunate, prosperous, or advanced in worldly circumstances.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with بِـ or with a thing or affair as the object of fortune or benefit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become great or highly esteemed in someone's eyes or in public estimation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with في عين or related expressions of esteem.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be serious or earnest rather than playful.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with في الأمر, في الكلام, or related constructions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strive, labor, exert oneself, or apply one's efforts vigorously.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of exertion in an affair, journey, course, or undertaking; the journey construction can imply hastening.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For an affair or event to distress or afflict someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction in which the event is treated as acting upon the person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a house or tent to drip or let fall drops.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized intransitive use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The making or weaving of stripes of different colors in a garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II verbal noun referring to the production of contrasting bands in cloth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contend with someone seriously over an affair, asserting one's position or exerting one's full effort.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with في الأمر; the expression can denote serious engagement or strenuous contention.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For palm trees to reach the time when their fruit is cut.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the ripening or harvest stage of date palms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To relinquish or forsake someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized reported construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make something new, put on something new, originate it, or renew it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of objects, garments, affairs, ablution, covenants, and similar things; the object or action is made new or begun afresh.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To establish or settle an affair firmly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional construction with an affair or case as object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For an affair or case to become easy or practicable.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reported alternative interpretation of the construction involving جَدَد, level ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a road or ground to become hard, level, and free of soft places; also, to reach or traverse such ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of movement onto or along firm, plain terrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become cut or cut off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reported original or literal development of the Form V verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For an udder or breast to lose its milk and become dry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a breast or udder that has become devoid of milk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become new, originate, or be renewed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used intransitively of a thing or affair that comes into being anew or is renewed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Good fortune, worldly prosperity, wealth, competence, or one's allotted means of subsistence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun of worldly advantage; it can denote a person's lot or resources received in life.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A grandfather or more remote ancestor; the father's or mother's father, and by extension an ancestor or ascendant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The feminine and extended ancestral uses are also recorded, with corresponding plural forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The side of anything.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use referring to an edge or lateral part.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well or water source.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reports variously describe it as a well with abundant water, a scanty or old well, or a water source at the edge of a desert.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Seriousness or earnestness, especially in speech or action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Contrasted with joking; also appears in oath-like and adjurative expressions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Striving, exertion, diligence, painstaking effort, or energy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of strenuous application in an affair; the adverbial expression جِدًّا intensifies a quality or action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Haste.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use in expressions describing someone as being in haste in an affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something carried out with seriousness and excess or intensity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to punishment or pace as an intensive characterization.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The bank or side of a river, or the shore of the sea.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may denote the part of a river nearest the land.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sign, mark, stripe, or distinguishing line.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A general nominal use for a visible mark in or on something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A beaten way, road, or track marked by lines or repeated passage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes paths or tracks forming lines on the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A way or manner of proceeding, or an opinion adopted concerning an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction for taking a course in an affair.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A rag or piece torn off from a garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions describing clothing with no such piece or rag upon it.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A collar or marked band around a dog's neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical or animal-related nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hard, level, smooth, rough, or spacious firm ground; also a conspicuous road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term covers terrain without soft places in which the feet sink; the reported descriptions vary between smooth and rough ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thin or fine sand sloping downward.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized terrain description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A growth or ganglion-like swelling on a camel's neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The cutting or harvesting of palm fruit, and the time or season for it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: جِدَاد is also reported with the same meaning; some usage distinguishes this harvest from the cutting of fruit generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ewe or other milch animal with little or no milk and a dry udder.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence includes both a restriction to ewes and a broader use for sheep or goats.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fat she-ass.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate animal-related nominal use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cut or cut off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An older adjectival or participial sense, distinct from the more common sense “new.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Something of which one has had no previous knowledge; unfamiliar or novel to a person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A semantic extension from what is new to the individual.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Death, or the beginning of death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal or archaic epithet, especially associated with Hudhayl.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The face or surface of the earth or ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominalized use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: What has been cut off, uprooted, or eradicated from palm trees and similar plants.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the resulting cut-off material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pad, stuffed piece, or felt attached beneath the boards or inner side of a horse's or camel's saddle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source notes that this form is post-classical in this specialized sense and gives other classical forms as alternatives.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cricket-like or grasshopper-like insect, especially one that creaks or leaps at night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry includes several identifications, including a small dark insect resembling a grasshopper or locust.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cutting or cutting off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The active participle of جَدَّ in its cutting sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Serious or earnest rather than joking.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used contrastively with play or jest.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Striving, laboring, or exerting oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of someone applying effort or energy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Producing a specified quantity of harvested dates or other agricultural yield.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized construction applied to land or palm trees according to their produce.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The main, central, even, or conspicuous part of a road; a main road or established route.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It can also mean a road generally, a road leading to water, or figuratively the right course of action.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having a part or parts cut off.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to animals whose ears, teats, or udder have been cut or severed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A milch animal whose milk has ceased and whose udder or teats have become dry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The reports include ewes, she-camels, and she-asses, sometimes attributing the dryness to injury.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman with a small or short breast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative or bodily description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dry or waterless; a desert without water or a year of drought and barren ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to desert land and, by extension, to a drought-stricken year.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most easy to walk or ride upon, plain, or level, said of a road.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative adjectival use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most fortunate.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel whose teats have been cut off through injury.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial animal description associated with injury from a tethering device.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A garment having stripes of different colors.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized adjectival use describing a striped cloak or garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quick-paced, said of a she-camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source reports uncertainty over whether the transmitted reading is مُجِدَّة or مُجَدَّة.

cautions: The noun جَدّ in 72:3 has both a majesty/greatness interpretation and a divine-effusion interpretation; these are retained as separate Quranic senses rather than collapsed into worldly fortune.
The Quranic form جُدَد in 35:27 is displayed under the supported singular citation form جُدَّة; the Classical evidence also records variant readings and related forms.

Several rare Classical entries preserve explicitly reported alternatives, including the contradictory descriptions of جُدّ as a well with abundant or scanty water and the uncertain reading of مُجِدّ in the quick-paced-camel phrase.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The quick-paced-camel phrase in lane-unit:jdd:46124:g1:sub2 is represented, but the source itself is uncertain whether the form should be read مُجِدَّة or مُجَدَّة.
